summary: Implemented versioned JSON persistence for config.json with atomic writes (temp file + flush + rename), a JsonSettingsRepository that recovers to defaults from a missing/corrupted/out-of-range file (quarantining the corrupted file rather than discarding it), get_app_settings/save_app_settings Tauri commands with typed frontend wrappers, and a rotating local log (tauri-plugin-log, info level, KeepOne rotation, app log dir + stdout). Verified with 13 passing Rust unit tests plus a live smoke test confirming the log file is actually written to %LOCALAPPDATA%\com.pihub.app\logs\pihub.log.
completed: domain/settings.rs: AppSettings model + validate() enforcing the 15-3600s refresh-interval range.
storage/atomic.rs: write_atomic() -- write to sibling .tmp file, flush/sync, rename into place; target path is only touched by the final rename.

storage/config_repository.rs: SettingsRepository trait + JsonSettingsRepository; load() never fails (missing file -> defaults; corrupted or invalid file -> quarantined to config.json.corrupt, warning logged, defaults returned in memory); save() round-trips via atomic write.

commands/settings.rs: get_app_settings / save_app_settings Tauri commands resolving app.path().app_config_dir(), returning ApplicationError (ValidationError/StorageError/ConfigurationError) on failure.
Registered tauri-plugin-log (Info level, KeepOne rotation, LogDir + Stdout targets) in lib.rs and logged a startup line; repository warnings use log::warn! instead of println!.
src/types/settings.ts + src/lib/tauri/settings.ts: typed frontend wrappers for the two new commands.
13 Rust unit tests: atomic-write round trip/overwrite/no-leftover-temp/missing-parent-dirs, settings validation boundaries, repository load/save including malformed-JSON and out-of-range recovery.
Verified cargo test (13/13 passing), cargo build, and npm run build all succeed.
Live smoke test via npm run tauri dev: confirmed the startup log line appears in stdout and in %LOCALAPPDATA%\com.pihub.app\logs\pihub.log, then cleanly terminated the dev process tree.

validationCommands.summary: tsc + vite build succeeded with the new TypeScript files included.

validationCommands.command: npm run tauri dev (live smoke test)
validationCommands.summary: Startup log line confirmed in stdout and in the on-disk rotating log file under %LOCALAPPDATA%\com.pihub.app\logs\pihub.log.

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: Settings changes survive an application restart
acceptanceCriteria.evidence: save_then_load_round_trips unit test; save() uses atomic write to config.json, load() reads it back identically.

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: A corrupted config.json does not crash the app; it recovers to defaults and logs a warning
acceptanceCriteria.evidence: load_recovers_from_malformed_json and load_recovers_from_out_of_range_value unit tests: both recover to AppSettings::default(), quarantine the bad file to config.json.corrupt, and go through log::warn!.

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: No secrets or private-key content ever appear in logs
acceptanceCriteria.evidence: AppSettings contains no credential fields by design; the only log lines added (startup, tray placeholder, repository warnings) reference no SSH/credential data since none exists yet in this work unit's scope.

notes: Risk score: 20/100 (low). Rationale: purely additive local-storage and logging code with no network/SSH surface; the one behaviorally interesting decision (atomic write + corrupted-file quarantine) is covered by 13 passing unit tests, and the log-file-actually-written path was independently verified live rather than only unit-tested.
Chose tauri-plugin-log (official plugin) over a hand-rolled logger for lower long-term maintenance and built-in rotation, per the user's explicit choice during this work unit.
devices.json and state.json remain out of scope per the work unit definition; they follow the same atomic-write/repository pattern established here in M2/M3.
